sources.note: Bibliography only. Lists for Hupla: Wurm & Hattori 1981 Map 4 ('[in GORGE dialect area of GRAND VALLEY DANI]'), Stuerzenhofecker 1990 Ts (anthropology), Silzer & Clouse 1991:50, Comrie 1992, Grimes 1992/1996/2000 ('Closely related to Lower Grand Valley Dani'; 3,000+ speakers, 1982 RBMU), Konrad 1996 (Uanang = Hupla). No linguistic description of any kind.

sources.citation: Bromley, H. Myron. 1981. A Grammar of Lower Grand Valley Dani. Pacific Linguistics C-63. Canberra: ANU. xiv+424 pp. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/145049, CC BY-SA).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology chapter; p. 67 n.1 and n.3 defer phonetics to Bromley 1961:49-52 and state that the hyphen marks 'a juncture separating a preceding fully-stressed form from a post-cliticised form with no stress or suppressed stress'; clitics 'are stressless or have suppressed stress and are thus phonologically dependent on a preceding normally stressed word nucleus'. LGV Dani only; Hupla not treated (space-insensitive search: no 'Hupla', 'Soba' hit is spurious).

sources.citation: Bromley, H. Myron. 1961. The Phonology of Lower Grand Valley Dani: A Comparative Structural Study of Skewed Phonemic Patterns. Verhandelingen KITLV 34. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. (Ch. II 'A survey of phonemic patterns of Dani dialects', pp. 6-19 = Glottolog ref 602157, the only reference Glottolog attaches to Hupla.) OAPEN open access.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For the Hupla-area variety ('Gorge Dani', GD, sec. 2.8 pp. 15-16: 'Down river from the LGV area, in the rough country along the gorge below the confluence with the Muki, lies a region called Basema'; based on 'a brief vocabulary check') it gives ONLY a consonant table and allophone notes -- nothing on stress. The book's only word-stress statement is for Lower Grand Valley Dani (lowe1415, Hupla's closest relative), sec. 3.132 p. 49: 'The phonological word consists of a syllable or group of syllables with only one primary word stress. sources.citation: Trenier, Sue and RBMU/World Team colleagues (Soba station, c. 1970s-2000s). Unpublished Hupla language materials: phonology/orthography statement, language-learning lessons, literacy primers underlying the Hupla Bible translation (completed c. 2011-2013). Possibly deposited with SIL Indonesia / UNCEN-SIL cooperative programme or World Team archives.

sources.note: The only first-hand linguistic analysis of Hupla known to exist (Wurm ed. 1977: 'Some study has been done of.. Hupla'; Ethnologue 1982 RBMU figures; vernacular literacy programme). An orthography statement would normally say whether stress is written/predictable.
